elements.element: Customer must have no obligation to provide Vendor terms based on, or no less favourable than, terms Customer provides to any third party.
elements.evidence: Section 7.2 expressly states that Customer is not obliged to offer Vendor terms no less favourable than its best terms for another technology supplier.

elements.element: The language must not preclude Vendor from granting MFN pricing or other MFN rights in Customer's favour.
elements.evidence: Neither § 7.2 nor § 12.3 prohibits Vendor from granting MFN rights to Customer; the operative negation addresses only an obligation imposed on Customer.

elements.element: If any MFN obligation burdens Customer, it must apply only to a specifically defined product.
elements.evidence: No MFN obligation burdening Customer remains under § 7.2, so the condition requiring a product limitation is demonstrably absent.

elements.element: If any MFN obligation burdens Customer, it must last no longer than 12 months.
elements.evidence: No MFN obligation burdening Customer remains under § 7.2, so there is no duration requiring limitation.

elements.element: If any MFN obligation burdens Customer, comparisons must be limited to reasonably comparable transactions, with exclusions or adjustments for material differences in circumstances.
elements.evidence: No MFN obligation burdening Customer remains under § 7.2, so no comparison mechanism is triggered; reasonable-comparison carve-outs are therefore unnecessary.

result.reason: The operative redline directly negates the Customer-burdening MFN and is consistent with § 12.3. It reaches the preferred position through a narrow change and leaves unrelated commercial terms intact. The drafting is effective but stylistically less clean than deleting § 7.2 entirely or stating affirmatively that Customer has no MFN obligation.
